subject: Liability cap: product-line sensitivity & proposed bucketed approach
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Liability cap: product-line sensitivity & proposed bucketed approach

Hi Sarah + ACME legal,

Thanks again for taking the time during Friday's negotiation call. Per our discussion, attached is a short sensitivity workbook (cap_sensitivity_model.xlsx) that maps three structuring options across your product lines:

- Single-contract total cap (aggregate across all products)
- Annualized cap (per 12-month trailing fees)
- Bucketed caps by product family (e.g., Core Search, Embed, Platform)

The workbook includes: fee history by product for the last 12 months, 3x and 5x multiples of fees scenarios, and sample language snippets for each approach. High-level rationale: the bucketed approach aims to align risk with observed spend patterns so that a large spike in one low-margin product doesn't bias the entire contract cap.

Key asks for ACME legal before we draft the formal redline:
1) Do you have a preference for annualized vs total cap for renewals?
2) Any minimum floor you expect (e.g., $250k)?
3) Any carveouts you need beyond the standard list (IP infringement, breach of confidentiality, bodily injury)?

Attaching the workbook and an initial redline placeholder (redline_msa_v2.docx) with the bucketed example pre-populated. Happy to walk through the numbers on a quick call.

Next step: if you can flag which approach you prefer, we’ll have legal produce a tracked redline targeted at your preference and circulate it back.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: cap_sensitivity_model.xlsx (xlsx, 48KB), redline_msa_v2.docx (docx, 32KB)

Subject: Re: Liability cap: product-line sensitivity & proposed bucketed approach

Karthik,

Thanks for the workbook — useful. A few quick points from ACME Legal (copied):

- We generally prefer an annualized cap that re-sets each 12 months tied to fees paid in that period. That aligns to our budgeting cycles and avoids front-loading liability if we ramp usage.
- We are wary of bucketed complexity — operationally ok but any bucketing must have clear definitions for what belongs in each product family and an agreed reconciliation process.
- Regarding multiples: 3x fees is a reasonable starting point. We would want to see the math that shows tail-risk for the largest product.
- Carveouts: in addition to the usual IP/Confidentiality, ACME needs an explicit carveout for regulatory fines and third-party indemnities (we'll supply sample language). Cyber/data breach carveout discussions: we prefer a higher cap for data incidents (not unlimited); typically we see a separate carveout cap or insurance offset.

Can Marissa or Laura put together a draft clause for an annualized cap with an optional product-bucket schedule? We’ll circle back with any redline language we’d propose.

– Sarah
Senior Counsel, ACME Corp.

Sarah / ACME legal — thanks for the direction. I put together the attached redline_msa_v2.docx with two parallel options in tracked changes:

Option A — Annualized cap
- Cap = greater of (i) $250,000 and (ii) 3x the fees paid in the prior 12 months for services under this Agreement.
- Reset occurs on each anniversary and applies prospectively.

Option B — Bucketed caps by product family
- Cap for each product family = 3x fees for that family in the prior 12 months, subject to a contract-level floor of $500,000.
- Reconciliation mechanism: monthly usage exports, 30-day dispute window, arbitration for unresolved allocation disputes.

Carveouts included (tracked):
- Liability for bodily injury or death;
- Liability resulting from wilful misconduct or gross negligence;
- Liability for IP infringement (subject to indemnity);
- Regulatory fines and third-party indemnities (explicit carveout language included).

Consequential damages: we preserved ACME's ask to carve out direct damages from consequential loss exclusion for certain categories (loss of business, lost profits) — however, we proposed a negotiated threshold: consequential damages remain excluded except for specific categories that are subject to the cap when caused by Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Rationale (short): the annualized option keeps billing parity and is simpler; bucketed is more precise for large multi-product customers but adds operational overhead. We left both in tracked changes so ACME can pick a route.

If ACME is comfortable with Option A we can produce a clean redline for signature quickly. If you want to preserve bucketed caps we’ll need a 1-hr ops/legal call to finalize product definitions and reconciliation timing.

Happy to jump on a call — propose Tue 10/13 09:00 PT.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa / Sarah — I’m available for the Tue 9am PT slot and have booked a calendar invite (sending separately). Laura from our finance team will join to speak to the fee history numbers and the proposed floors.

One practical note from sales: ACME has one very large monthly consumer product where usage can spike seasonally. If we go annualized there is a risk ACME is effectively self-insuring a short sharp spike — bucketed with a reconciliation may be the fairest outcome, but I appreciate the ops ask.

Agenda for the call:
- Walk through the sensitivity workbook (Marissa/Laura)
- Agree on core carveouts and whether data incidents get a separate carveout cap or insurance-first approach
- Decide on annualized vs bucketed and next steps for redlines

Thanks,
Karthik

Marissa / Karthik — ACME legal confirmed via the call earlier that we prefer Option A (annualized cap) with one modification: data breach incidents will be handled under a separate data-incident cap equal to the greater of (i) 5x the fees attributable to the product in the prior 12 months, or (ii) $1,000,000, subject to insurance offsets. We will circulate a short redline to lock language around insurance subrogation and offsets.

We appreciate Redwood keeping a $250k floor in the annualized model. Once Marissa sends the clean version, we’ll do a final check and route for signature (DocuSign link to follow).
